title: TO THE THIRD AND FOURTH GENERATION

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin
of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, but
showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my
commandments.'" - Ex 20:5b-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two difficult words here, and we should face them honestly.

First, "jealous." In people this is usually a vice, but God's jealousy is not
petty possessiveness. It is the right response of a husband to a wife's
unfaithfulness. It would be strange, not noble, for a spouse to be indifferent.
God's jealousy is love that refuses to share what belongs to it.

Second, the generations. This is not saying God punishes innocent children for
their parents' sins. Ezekiel addresses that misunderstanding directly and denies
it: "The one who sins is the one who will die" (Ezek 18:20). Rather, this
describes what actually happens. Sin runs downhill through families. Idolatry,
bitterness, addiction, and violence shape the households that follow.

Anyone who has seen a family pattern repeat across generations knows this is
simply true.

But look at the asymmetry, because it is the point. Three or four generations of
consequence; a thousand generations of love. That is not balance. That is mercy
overwhelmingly outweighing judgment.

And patterns can break. In Christ, a chain that has run for generations can end
with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What pattern in your family would you like to see end with you?
2. Does God's mercy feel larger to you than His judgment, as this verse
   describes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your love runs a thousand generations deep. Break in me
what should not pass on. Amen.
